thread:
maria: Heads-up — seeing big NVMe IOPS spikes on several eu-west1-gpu nodes during the nightly cleanup. Nodes hitting DiskPressure, gpu-provisioner stalls when trying to move pods. Anyone else?

devin: Ack. Grafana shows sustained ~120k read IOPS on nvme0 on 3 nodes starting ~01:10 UTC. p99 IO latency spiked to ~85ms. Multiple pods stuck ContainerCreating with DiskPressure.

maria: Log snippets from kubelet/journal: 
```
kernel: nvme nvme0: I/O 0x7f failed, status: 0x1
kubelet: eviction manager: node has disk pressure (availableInodes=0)
journalctl -u ephemeral-cleaner: deleting /var/lib/ephemeral/model-cache-abc... rm: I/O error
```

kai: Confirmed — ephemeral-cleaner kicked off at 01:05 and spins N parallel scrubs (cpu_count). That plus large nightly batch downloads (model layers) is likely saturating the queue depth.

ashley: Can we throttle the cleaner? Current helm values have concurrency=6. Suggest dropping to 1 and adding a rate-limit flag (e.g., --rate-limit=40MB/s) until we understand wear.

devin: Also seeing SMART warnings on nvme0: "Media and Data Integrity Errors" on eu-west1-gpu-22. Opening a hardware RMA. Could be early wear on that device.

ops-bot: @maria created ticket INF-4722: "eu-west1 nvme iops spike / DiskPressure - investigation" and scheduled temporary cordon for eu-west1-gpu-21 at 02:15 UTC.

srebot: Automated mitigation applied: bumped kubelet ephemeral-storage eviction threshold to 10% on affected ASG and disabled aggressive ephemeral reclaim for 30m.

kai: Short-term plan: cordon affected nodes, reschedule heavy batch jobs to us-west2 for the next 24h, reduce ephemeral-cleaner concurrency, and add an off-peak window. Medium-term: lower per-node batch concurrency or prefix-cache model artifacts to cut read amplification.

maria: I just updated helm chart values and triggered a rollback/rollout: ephemeralCleaner.concurrency=1, ephemeralCleaner.rateLimitMB=40. Rolling restart in progress.

devin: After the change IOPS dropped to ~18k and p99 IO latency back down to ~12ms on two nodes. eu-west1-gpu-22 still shows read errors; RMA in flight.

ashley: Cost note: replacing NVMe under warranty is free but operational swap cost and lost capacity matter. If we consider switching instance type (instance-store vs attached NVMe), compute cost delta may offset savings from fewer failures. I'll run a quick cost delta for 3/6/12 month windows.

maria: Action items: 
- devin: open hardware RMA for eu-west1-gpu-22 (INF-4723)
- kai: add off-peak window for cleaner (02:30-05:30 UTC) and add a concurrency flag in helm values
- ashley: run cost delta instance-store vs attached-NVMe by EOW
- infra: add precheck in gpu-provisioner to skip nodes with recent SMART errors

devin: INF-4723 opened and assigned to hardware team. I'll continue monitoring overnight and post updates.

ashley: Heads-up to sales: dedicated capacity provisioning in eu-west1 may slip by 1-2 days while we heal the fleet. I'll notify account owners.

maria: Thanks team — great quick triage :thumbsup: We should also add a postmortem if RMA rate is >3% this quarter.

ops-bot: Note: cordon for eu-west1-gpu-21 removed at 03:40 UTC after successful reschedule of pods.

maria: Will follow up tomorrow with numbers and a brief runbook for the cleaner.
